title: triad-sdk-credential-window-and-stream-flow-refinements
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: customers reported sporadic 401s during long pull/stream sessions and awkward ergonomics for checking stream liveness. This PR introduces a lightweight credential 'sliding window' that normalizes prefetch timing across SDKs, plus two small stream ergonomics helpers (peek_end and wait_for_end) and instrumentation to correlate reauth events with stream traces. Changes span Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs and docs. What changed: 1) Credential sliding window: add a tunable lease_window and prefetch_margin to SDK credential providers so refresh is deterministic across clock skew and latency. Default profile keeps behavior identical but allows operators to reduce reauth jitter for long-lived streams. 2) Stream ergonomics: add Stream.peek_end() to poll if the upstream finished without consuming tokens, and Stream.wait_for_end(timeout) as a convenience awaitable. Implementations are fully non-blocking and optimized for the host runtime (asyncio/promises/goroutines). 3) Telemetry: emit stream.reauth.attempt and stream.reauth.success spans and attach credential_window arg for easier debugging in Console. 4) Cross-SDK parity work: align arg names and defaults across py/ts/go, bump versions (py 0.12.4 -> 0.12.5, ts 1.6.2 -> 1.6.3, go v1.5.1 -> v1.5.2). 5) Tests and docs: add unit and integration tests to cover the window edge cases and update quickstart examples and changelog. Rollout plan: feature guarded behind SDK feature flag (CRED_WINDOW_ALPHA); default is off in existing published builds so behavior is opt-in for early adopters. Impact: reduces observed 401 spikes during sustained streams, clarifies telemetry for SRE, and gives app authors ergonomic primitives for stream lifecycle. Checklist: - [x] API signatures reviewed across SDKs - [x] Telemetry schema bump registered - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test with dedicated runtime - [x] Docs/quickstart updated - [x] Version bumps staged

review_comments: Diego Morales: Can we make the default prefetch_margin relative (percentage) instead of absolute seconds? Some customers have very long TTLs.
Ava Chen: Discussed offline with Diego; added margin_mode config (absolute_seconds | percentage) and left default as absolute_seconds for backward compatibility. Added docs to explain tradeoffs.
Priya Kapoor: In TS, peek_end currently allocates an extra promise on each poll; can we reuse an internal pending promise to reduce churn?
Ava Chen: Updated TS implementation to reuse a single deferred promise for the peek path, added benchmark microtest, results show ~10% fewer allocations under steady polling.
Liam O'Neill: CI showed flakey TestStreamTimeout in Go initially — root cause was a race on context cancellation. Please ensure context teardown ordering is deterministic.
Ava Chen: Fixed Go test by moving cancel after pipeline drain; reran CI and test stabilized.
release_notes: Added optional credential sliding window and two stream lifecycle helpers (peek_end, wait_for_end). Telemetry now surfaces stream.reauth spans. SDKs bumped: Python -> 0.12.5, TypeScript -> 1.6.3, Go -> v1.5.2. Feature guarded behind CRED_WINDOW_ALPHA.
notes: Behavior is opt-in by default. We plan to monitor stream.reauth.* events for two weeks post-release before recommending enabling globally for customers with high-volume long-lived streams.
